_meta.name: sprint-emancipate-resume-machine
_meta.description: Build resume-machine from scratch per north-star v1.1.0: pure-Python ingest via BeautifulSoup4+lxml, structured skills correlation, two-file output (correlation always overwritten, cover letter written once), deterministic orchestration, and a vanilla HTML/ES2020 UX served by a Python HTTP server.
_meta.sprint_goal: Deliver a fully operational local resume-machine that ingests HTML job postings, correlates them against a structured skills index, adapts output to domain-specific role templates, and exposes a browser-based UX with year/month/keyword navigation and print-to-PDF — all in pure Python with no Node.js runtime.
_meta.pd-004-override: skills-index.json remains in v2.3.0 facet_catalog format (operator decision C). The correlator adapts via _build_facet_lookup(). north-star skills_index_schema requires a follow-up update to reflect this.

phases.title: Migration — Salvage, Clean, and Reconcile
phases.description: Execute all pre-build housekeeping before writing any new code: delete the Node.js pipeline and shell shims (pd-001), clean up root-level duplicate shim scripts, restructure role templates into the sprint format, strip placeholder fields from resume.source.json, reconcile config.yaml keys, and extend naming_utils.py with the path functions the build phases require. References migration-manifest.json for per-file port/drop detail. All p0 tasks must be complete before p1 begins.

tasks.title: Delete Node.js files and shell orchestration
tasks.what: Remove all files identified as DROP in migration-manifest.json: Node.js scripts (extract-html-data.js, preprocess-resume.js, sanitize.js, debug-sanitize.js), shell scripts (batch-process.sh), Python subprocess orchestrators (py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py), and the standalone skill analyzer (py_job_skill_analyzer.py). Also remove data files that belong to the dropped pipeline (resume-machine-queue.json, resume.unique-data.json, role-based-templates/default/).

steps: Delete all files listed in migration-manifest.json drop-001 through drop-009 in the order given.
Delete the role-based-templates/default/ directory and its contents (drop-011 partial).
Delete resume.unique-data.json (drop-009).
Delete resume-machine-queue.json (drop-008).
Run 'find scripts -name "*.js" -o -name "*.sh"' to verify no Node.js or shell files remain.
Run 'git status' and confirm all deleted files appear as deletions with no unintended removals.

tasks.done_when: No .js or .sh files exist anywhere under scripts/. No resume-machine-queue.json, resume.unique-data.json, or role-based-templates/default/ exist. git status shows only deletions in this batch.

tasks.title: Delete root-level script shims
tasks.what: Remove the three root-level shim files in scripts/ that redirect to subdirectory implementations (migration-manifest.json drop-007). These cause os.execv loops and import confusion once the subdirectory versions are the canonical implementations.
tasks.how: Delete scripts/py_skill_job_correlator.py, scripts/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py, and scripts/config_manager.py (root-level shims). Then create the src/ directory structure and move implementations to their canonical locations: move scripts/data_processing/py_extract_jobs.py → src/data/py_extract_jobs.py; move scripts/data_processing/py_skill_job_correlator.py → src/data/py_skill_job_correlator.py; move scripts/template_management/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py → src/models/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py; move scripts/utilities/config_manager.py → src/utils/config_manager.py; move scripts/utilities/naming_utils.py → src/utils/naming_utils.py; move config.yaml → config/config.yaml; move skills-index.json → data/skills-index.json; move resume.source.json → data/resume.source.json; move role-based-templates/ → data/role-based-templates/; move jobbankjobs/ → data/jobbankjobs/; move ux/resume-machine.html → src/api/resume-machine.html. Remove empty remnant directories (scripts/data_processing/, scripts/utilities/, scripts/template_management/, scripts/orchestration/, ux/).
tasks.done_when: Root shims deleted. src/data/, src/models/, src/utils/, src/api/, config/, and data/ directories all exist and contain the ported files. scripts/ root has only process.py (to be written in p4). No scripts/data_processing/, scripts/utilities/, scripts/template_management/, or scripts/orchestration/ subdirectories remain.

tasks.title: Restructure role-based-templates to sprint format
tasks.what: Convert the 5 existing role template files from the {featured_languages, highlight_1...N} format to the sprint's {domain, keywords[], facet_types[], highlights[]} format. Rename files from resume.{domain}.json to {domain}.json. Drop crm, defaults, and YAML siblings. Note: backend, frontend, fullstack templates are ABSENT — they are created in p2-t1, not here.

steps: For each of ai (from resume.ai.json), database, devops, manager, sted: create a new data/role-based-templates/{domain}.json with: domain = filename stem; keywords = sorted array from DOMAIN_PATTERNS in src/models/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py (for ai use ml_ai entry); facet_types = sorted array from DOMAIN_PATTERNS; highlights = array built from resume.{domain}.json highlight_1..N values with all and tags stripped. If the file has fewer than 6 highlights, add de-HTML'd strings from DOMAIN_PATTERNS highlights until 6 are present.

For sted: no DOMAIN_PATTERNS entry exists. Use resume.sted.json highlights as-is (strip HTML). Add a '_note' field: 'keywords and facet_types require operator input; sted domain detection will fall back to DEFAULT_DOMAIN until populated.'
Delete resume.crm.json (drop-010), resume.defaults.json, resume.defaults.yaml, resume.ai.yaml, resume.database.yaml (drop-011).
Delete the source resume.*.json files after the new {domain}.json files are written and verified as valid JSON.
Verify: exactly 5 .json files exist under data/role-based-templates/ (ai.json, database.json, devops.json, manager.json, sted.json). No resume.*.json, no .yaml files, no default/ subdirectory.

tasks.done_when: data/role-based-templates/ contains exactly 5 valid JSON files (ai.json, database.json, devops.json, manager.json, sted.json). Each file has domain, keywords (array), facet_types (array), highlights (array, min 4 entries). No HTML tags present in any highlights string. No resume.*.json or .yaml files remain.
tasks.notes: backend, frontend, fullstack templates are absent and will be created in p2-t1. The adapter will fall back to DEFAULT_DOMAIN ('fullstack') for those roles until p2-t1 is complete.

tasks.title: Strip placeholders from resume.source.json
tasks.what: Remove the 'summary' field (contains {{featured_languages}}, {{highlight_1..4}} placeholders) and the 'coverLetter' field (contains {{cover_letter_content}} placeholder) from resume.source.json. The sprint derives summary from correlation highlights[] at render time in resume-machine.html; cover letter content comes from the separate letter-*.json file.
tasks.how: Open resume.source.json. Remove the top-level 'summary' key if its value contains any {{...}} template placeholders. Remove the top-level 'coverLetter' key entirely. Verify no remaining {{...}} strings exist anywhere in the file. Save and validate JSON.
tasks.done_when: data/resume.source.json is valid JSON; no {{...}} placeholder strings appear anywhere in the file; the file retains basics, work[], education[], and skills[] sections with real candidate data.

tasks.title: Reconcile config.yaml keys
tasks.what: Update config.yaml to use the key names expected by the sprint spec and drop keys that belong to the eliminated Node.js pipeline.

steps: Rename 'input_dir' → 'jobbankjobs_dir'.
Add 'skills_index_path: data/skills-index.json' if not present.
Add 'resume_source_path: data/resume.source.json' if not present.

Remove or comment out: 'output_dir' (replaced by artifacts_dir if needed), 'queue_file', 'unique_data_file', 'skip_extract', 'dry_run', 'pdf_naming_template', 'theme' — all belong to the dropped pipeline.
Keep: 'candidate_name', 'role_templates_dir', 'log_level'.
Verify config/config.yaml has exactly these top-level keys: candidate_name, jobbankjobs_dir, skills_index_path, resume_source_path, role_templates_dir, log_level.

tasks.done_when: config/config.yaml contains candidate_name, jobbankjobs_dir, skills_index_path, resume_source_path, role_templates_dir, and log_level as top-level keys. No pipeline-specific keys (queue_file, theme, pdf_naming_template, unique_data_file) remain.

tasks.title: Extend naming_utils.py with sprint path functions
tasks.what: Add slugify (alias), job_json_path(), correlation_json_path(), and cover_letter_json_path() to src/utils/naming_utils.py per migration-manifest.json port-004. The existing sanitize_for_filename() function is preserved as-is.

steps: Add at module level after sanitize_for_filename: slugify = sanitize_for_filename
Add job_json_path(base_dir: str, year: int, month: int, day: int, slug: str) → str: return f'{base_dir}/{year}/{month:02d}/{day:02d}/{slug}.json'

Add correlation_json_path(base_dir: str, year: int, month: int, day: int, candidate: str, employer: str, title: str) → str: employer_slug = slugify(employer); title_slug = slugify(title); return f'{base_dir}/{year}/{month:02d}/{day:02d}/resume-{candidate}-{employer_slug}-{title_slug}.json'
Add cover_letter_json_path() with identical signature and logic but 'letter-' prefix.

Verify: all four functions are importable; slugify('Software Engineer (Senior)') returns 'software-engineer-senior'; correlation_json_path and cover_letter_json_path return paths with their respective prefixes and no filesystem access occurs.

tasks.done_when: from src.utils.naming_utils import slugify, job_json_path, correlation_json_path, cover_letter_json_path succeeds. slugify('Software Engineer (Senior)') returns 'software-engineer-senior'. cover_letter_json_path and correlation_json_path return paths with 'letter-' and 'resume-' prefixes respectively in the correct datestamped directory.

tasks.title: Drop skills-schema.json and YAML siblings
tasks.what: Delete skills-schema.json (the standalone JSON Schema v2.3.0 file) and any remaining YAML files not yet removed in p0-t1/p0-t3.
tasks.how: Delete skills-schema.json. Verify no .yaml files remain in the project root or its subdirectories (role-based-templates .yaml siblings were removed in p0-t3; confirm none were missed).
tasks.done_when: skills-schema.json does not exist. No .yaml files exist anywhere in the project root or subdirectories except config/config.yaml.

phases.title: Foundation — Utilities, Configuration, and Static Data
phases.description: Establish the shared utility layer (logging, config, naming), application configuration, the structured skills catalog (pd-004), and base candidate data. All downstream phases import from this layer. utilities/ has no internal dependencies.

tasks.title: Create config.yaml
tasks.what: Write the application configuration file recording candidate_name, jobbankjobs_dir, skills_index_path, resume_source_path, and role_templates_dir.
tasks.how: Define exactly five top-level YAML keys. All path values are relative to the project root. candidate_name defaults to an empty string (overridable at runtime via --name flag).
tasks.done_when: config/config.yaml exists under the config/ directory and contains all five keys; the four path fields have non-empty string values.

tasks.title: Create logging_manager.py
tasks.what: Implement get_logger(name: str) → logging.Logger that returns a named child logger with a StreamHandler emitting to stdout at a configurable level. Must be importable with no side effects.
tasks.how: Use Python stdlib logging only. Configure a root 'resume-machine' logger once on first call using a module-level guard. Child loggers inherit the handler. Default level: INFO. Format: '%(asctime)s [%(name)s] %(levelname)s %(message)s'.
tasks.done_when: from src.utils.logging_manager import get_logger; logger = get_logger('test'); logger.info('ok') emits exactly one line to stdout containing the timestamp, logger name, level, and message. Importing the module alone produces no output.

tasks.title: Create config_manager.py
tasks.what: Implement load_config() → dict that locates config/config.yaml by resolving relative to the project root, parses it with PyYAML, and returns all path values as absolute resolved strings.

steps: Resolve the project root using pathlib.Path(__file__).parents[2] (three levels up from src/utils/).
Load YAML with yaml.safe_load(). Do not use yaml.load().
For each of the four path keys (jobbankjobs_dir, skills_index_path, resume_source_path, role_templates_dir), resolve the value against the project root and return the absolute path string.
Raise FileNotFoundError with a descriptive message including the expected path if config/config.yaml is absent.
Log the resolved config dict at DEBUG via logging_manager.get_logger('resume-machine.config').

tasks.done_when: load_config() returns a dict with all five keys; all four path values are absolute pathlib-resolved strings; calling it when config.yaml is absent raises FileNotFoundError whose message contains the expected path.

tasks.title: Create naming_utils.py
tasks.what: Implement four pure functions for consistent slug and output-path generation used by the extractor, correlator, and server.

steps: slugify(text: str) → str: lowercase; replace all non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens; collapse consecutive hyphens into one; strip leading and trailing hyphens.
job_json_path(base_dir: str, year: int, month: int, day: int, slug: str) → str: returns '{base_dir}/{year}/{month:02d}/{day:02d}/{slug}.json'.

correlation_json_path(base_dir: str, year: int, month: int, day: int, candidate: str, employer: str, title: str) → str: applies slugify to employer and title; returns path to 'resume-{candidate}-{slugified_employer}-{slugified_title}.json' inside the datestamped directory.

cover_letter_json_path(base_dir: str, year: int, month: int, day: int, candidate: str, employer: str, title: str) → str: identical structure to correlation_json_path but with the 'letter-' prefix instead of 'resume-'.

tasks.done_when: slugify('Software Engineer (Senior)') returns 'software-engineer-senior'; correlation_json_path and cover_letter_json_path return paths in the correct datestamped directory with their respective prefixes; all four functions are importable from src.utils.naming_utils and produce correct output without any filesystem access.

tasks.title: Create skills-index.json
tasks.what: Populate the skills catalog as a JSON array of structured skill objects per pd-004. Every object must carry name and proficiency; domain, years_experience, and verified are optional.
tasks.how: Write a representative initial array covering multiple domains. Each object: { "name": string, "proficiency": "expert"|"proficient"|"familiar", "domain": string (optional), "years_experience": integer (optional), "verified": boolean (optional) }. Include at least 20 entries spanning devops, backend, frontend, and ai domains.
tasks.done_when: data/skills-index.json is a valid JSON array with at least 20 entries; every object has a non-empty name string and a proficiency value of exactly 'expert', 'proficient', or 'familiar'; no other proficiency values are present.

tasks.title: Create resume.source.json
tasks.what: Write the base candidate data file containing basics, work, education, and skills sections per resume_source_schema. This file is returned verbatim by GET /api/resume.
tasks.how: Populate all required_sections: basics (name, email, phone, location, profiles array of {network, username, url}); work (array of {company, position, startDate, endDate, summary}); education (array of {institution, studyType, area, startDate, endDate}); skills (array of {name, level, keywords[]}).
tasks.done_when: data/resume.source.json is valid JSON containing all four required_sections; basics.name and basics.email are non-empty strings; work and education are non-empty arrays.

phases.title: Template Management — Role Templates and Domain Adapter
phases.description: Create domain-specific role template JSON files for all eight known domains and implement py_adapter_correlator_to_template exposing infer_domain(). This layer depends on utilities only and is imported by the correlator in the next phase.

tasks.title: Create role-based-templates for all 8 domains
tasks.what: Write one JSON file per known domain (devops, backend, frontend, fullstack, manager, ai, database, sted) conforming to role_template_schema: domain string, keywords array, facet_types array, highlights array of 6+ plain-text strings (no HTML).

steps: For each of the 8 domains, create data/role-based-templates/{domain}.json.
domain field must exactly match the filename stem (e.g. 'devops' in devops.json).
keywords: 10 or more domain-relevant technology and skill terms that the adapter will match against correlation term values.
facet_types: list the correlation tag labels most relevant to this domain, chosen from LEAD_STRENGTH, SOLID_MATCH, PARTIAL_MATCH, UNTESTED_CLAIM, GAP_ADJACENCY, HARD_GAP.
highlights: 6 to 10 plain-text strings describing candidate strengths for this domain. No HTML tags. No markdown. No bracketed placeholders.

tasks.done_when: Exactly 8 JSON files exist under data/role-based-templates/, one for each known domain. Each file is valid JSON; domain matches the filename stem; keywords, facet_types, and highlights are non-empty arrays; highlights has at least 6 entries; no HTML appears in any highlights string.

tasks.title: Create py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py
tasks.what: Implement infer_domain(correlation_data: dict, role_templates_dir: str) → dict returning { domain: str, featured_languages: list[str], highlights: list[str] }. This function is imported by the correlator after facets are computed.

steps: Load all *.json files from role_templates_dir at call time (no module-level cache); raise FileNotFoundError if the directory is empty.
Score each template by counting how many of its keywords appear as term values in correlation_data['correlations'][]. Higher score wins.
On tie, select the alphabetically first domain name.

featured_languages: collect unique term values from correlations whose tag is LEAD_STRENGTH or SOLID_MATCH and whose term case-insensitively matches a hardcoded language list: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Java, Rust, C++, SQL, Bash, Ruby.
highlights: return up to 6 strings from the winning template's highlights array.
Return { 'domain': str, 'featured_languages': list, 'highlights': list }.

tasks.done_when: from src.models.py_adapter_correlator_to_template import infer_domain; calling infer_domain({'correlations': [{'term': 'Python', 'type': 'language', 'tag': 'LEAD_STRENGTH', 'notes': ''}]}, role_templates_dir) returns a dict with domain, featured_languages, and highlights keys; highlights contains at most 6 items; featured_languages contains 'Python'.

phases.title: Data Processing — Ingest and Correlation
phases.description: Implement the two core pipeline scripts. The extractor uses BeautifulSoup4+lxml with no Node.js (pd-001). The correlator writes exactly two output files per pd-002: correlation JSON always overwritten; cover letter JSON written only when absent.

tasks.title: Create py_extract_jobs.py
tasks.what: Implement the ingest script that parses HTML job posting files using BeautifulSoup4 with the lxml backend — no Node.js, no browser automation (pd-001) — and writes one job JSON per HTML file conforming to job_json_schema.

steps: Accept a single positional argument: input_dir (path to the {year}/{month:02d}/{day:02d}/ directory). Derive year, month, day integers from the three rightmost path components.
Enumerate all *.html files in input_dir. Exit 1 with a clear message if none are found.
For each HTML file: open in binary mode, decode utf-8, parse with BeautifulSoup(content, 'lxml').

Extract all required job_json_schema fields: job_title, employer, location, job_posting.required_skills (array of strings), job_posting.additional_skills (array of strings), job_posting.responsibilities (array of strings), job_posting.overview (string), job_posting.specialization (string).
Generate slug = naming_utils.slugify(job_title).
Write output JSON to naming_utils.job_json_path(base_dir, year, month, day, slug). Create parent directories with exist_ok=True.
Log each file at INFO via logging_manager.get_logger('resume-machine.ingest'). Log parse errors at ERROR and continue to the next file.
Exit 0 if all files succeed.

tasks.done_when: python -m src.data.py_extract_jobs data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01 exits with code 0; one .json output file is written per .html file in the directory; every output JSON contains all required_fields from job_json_schema with non-null string or array values; no Node.js process is invoked at any point.

tasks.title: Create py_skill_job_correlator.py
tasks.what: Implement the correlator that reads a job JSON and skills-index.json (array of skill objects per pd-004), generates correlation facets, calls infer_domain, and writes exactly two output files per pd-002: correlation JSON (always overwritten) and cover letter JSON (written only when absent).

steps: Accept positional argument job_json_path. Accept --name flag to override candidate_name from config.
Load job JSON, skills-index.json array, and config via config_manager.load_config().

Correlate: for each skill in skills-index.json, check whether skill.name (or its prefix) appears in job_posting.required_skills or job_posting.additional_skills. Assign tag: LEAD_STRENGTH (required + expert), SOLID_MATCH (required + proficient), PARTIAL_MATCH (additional, any proficiency), UNTESTED_CLAIM (required + familiar), GAP_ADJACENCY (adjacent domain skill not directly required), HARD_GAP (required skill absent from index entirely).

Derive summary: total_correlations = len(correlations); hard_gaps_count = count of entries where tag == 'HARD_GAP'; tag_distribution = dict mapping each tag to its count; hard_gaps = list of { term, context } for each HARD_GAP entry.
Call infer_domain(correlation_data, config['role_templates_dir']) imported from py_adapter_correlator_to_template. Merge returned domain, featured_languages, highlights into correlation_data.

Populate metadata: job_title, employer, location (from job JSON), generated_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z', job_json = absolute path to source job JSON, skills_index = absolute path to skills-index.json.
Write correlation JSON to naming_utils.correlation_json_path(...). Always overwrite without checking existence.

Resolve cover letter path via naming_utils.cover_letter_json_path(...). If the file does not exist: generate cover letter JSON with opening (string), value_proposition (string), relevant_experience (array of up to 5 strings derived from highlights), closing (string). Write it. If the file already exists: do nothing — do not read, do not modify.
Expose correlate_job(job_json_path: str, candidate_name: str | None = None) → None as an importable function for use by process.py.

tasks.done_when: Running the script against a job JSON exits 0; correlation JSON is written and contains all required_fields from correlation_json_schema; cover letter JSON is written on the first run and contains opening, value_proposition, relevant_experience, and closing; running the script a second time does not alter the cover letter JSON (verified by mtime or SHA-256 before and after); correlate_job is importable as a standalone function.

phases.title: Orchestration — Batch Processing Entry Point
phases.description: Implement process.py, the CLI orchestrator that drives batch or single-file correlation by calling correlate_job as an imported function (never subprocess). Supports --dir, --file, --dry-run, and --name flags per the north-star CLI wiring.

tasks.title: Create process.py
tasks.what: Implement the orchestration entry point that accepts --dir, --file, --dry-run, and --name, discovers job JSON files, calls correlate_job as an imported function (no subprocess), and reports per-file results.

steps: Parse CLI with argparse: --dir (directory path), --file (single job JSON path), --dry-run (boolean flag), --name (string, optional). Exactly one of --dir or --file must be supplied; raise a usage error otherwise.
File discovery for --dir: collect all *.json files in the given directory whose filename does not start with 'resume-' or 'letter-' (job JSONs only, excluding correlation and cover letter outputs).
If --dry-run: print each discovered file path, print total count, exit 0 without writing any files.
For each discovered job JSON: call correlate_job(path, args.name) imported from src.data.py_skill_job_correlator. Catch and log all exceptions at ERROR without halting the batch.
Log batch start (file count) and completion (success count, error count) at INFO via logging_manager.get_logger('resume-machine.orchestration').
Exit 0 if all files succeed. Exit 1 if any file raised an exception.
No subprocess.run, os.system, or any shell invocation is present in the implementation.

tasks.done_when: python scripts/process.py --dir data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01 exits 0 and writes correlation and cover letter files for all job JSONs in the target directory; python scripts/process.py --dry-run --dir data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01 prints paths and exits 0 without writing any files; python scripts/process.py --file data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01/sample.json processes exactly one file; no subprocess or shell invocation appears in the source.

phases.title: UX — HTTP Server and Browser Interface
phases.description: Implement serve.py (stdlib-only Python HTTP server with three API endpoints and path-traversal protection) and resume-machine.html (vanilla HTML/CSS/ES2020, no build step) with year/month/keyword navigation, cover letter toggle, and print-to-PDF per pd-003.

tasks.title: Create serve.py
tasks.what: Implement a stdlib-only Python HTTP server on localhost:8080 serving resume-machine.html as the root and exposing GET /api/jobs, GET /api/resume, and GET /api/correlation. /api/correlation must validate that the supplied path resolves within data/jobbankjobs/ before reading.

steps: Use http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler. No third-party HTTP framework.
Accept optional --port argument defaulting to 8080. Log the bound address at INFO on startup.
GET /: Read src/api/resume-machine.html relative to the project root. Respond 200 with Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.

GET /api/jobs?year=YYYY[&month=MM]: Walk data/jobbankjobs/{year}/{month:02d}/ (or all months under {year}/ when month is absent). Collect all files matching the resume-* pattern. For each, read JSON and extract path (relative to the project root, i.e. data/jobbankjobs/{year}/{month:02d}/{day:02d}/{filename} — this value is passed directly as the path parameter to /api/correlation), job_title, employer, location, domain. Return a JSON array sorted by date directory descending (newest first). Content-Type: application/json.
GET /api/resume: Read data/resume.source.json. Return its content as JSON.

GET /api/correlation?path=...: Resolve the path parameter against the project root using pathlib.Path.resolve(). Reject with HTTP 400 if the resolved path does not begin with the resolved data/jobbankjobs/ directory (path-traversal guard). Load correlation JSON. Derive the companion cover letter path by replacing the 'resume-' filename prefix with 'letter-' (e.g. data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01/resume-x-y-z.json → data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01/letter-x-y-z.json). If the cover letter file exists, merge its fields (opening, value_proposition, relevant_experience, closing) into the response dict. Return unified JSON.
Set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all /api/* responses.
Log each request method and path at INFO via logging_manager.get_logger('resume-machine.server').
Return 404 for unrecognized paths. Return 400 for path-traversal attempts.

tasks.done_when: python -m src.api.serve starts and logs 'Serving on localhost:8080'; GET /api/jobs?year=2025 returns a valid JSON array; GET /api/resume returns JSON containing a basics.name field; GET /api/correlation?path=data/jobbankjobs/2025/05/01/resume-x-y-z.json returns a merged object containing both correlation fields and cover letter fields; GET /api/correlation?path=../../etc/passwd returns HTTP 400; the implementation contains no third-party imports beyond the stdlib.

tasks.title: Create resume-machine.html
tasks.what: Implement the single-page browser UX in vanilla HTML/CSS/ES2020 (no build step, no framework): filters panel with year select, optional month select, keyword search input, and cover letter toggle; scrollable job results list with empty-state message; printable area with a cover letter page followed by a resume page.

steps: On DOMContentLoaded: populate the year <select> with current year ± 2 years, defaulting to current year. Fetch /api/jobs?year={current_year} and render the job list. Cache the /api/resume response after the first fetch.
Year <select> change: fetch /api/jobs?year=YYYY. Reapply the current keyword filter client-side.
Month <select>: blank option by default (no month filter active). Selecting a month fetches /api/jobs?year=YYYY&month=MM. Keyword filter reapplied client-side.

Keyword <input>: on every input event, filter the rendered job list in-place without any network request. When the filtered list is empty, display the message 'No results for current filters.' in the results area.

Job row click: fetch /api/correlation?path={row.dataset.path} and the cached /api/resume. Hydrate cover letter panel with opening, value_proposition, relevant_experience[] as list items, and closing. Hydrate resume panel with: contact block from basics; summary paragraph from highlights[0] through highlights[2]; work history from work[]; skills list from skills[].name; education from education[].
Cover letter toggle: a checkbox, checked by default. On change, toggle a 'cover-letter--hidden' CSS class on the cover letter section. No network request.
Print: set document.title to '{employer} — {job_title}.pdf', then call window.print().

@media print: page size Letter 8.5in × 11in, margins 0.7in; cover letter section receives page-break-after: always; filters panel and results list are hidden; body font-family: 'Source Serif Pro', serif; UI element font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif.

tasks.done_when: Opening http://localhost:8080 renders a filters panel with year select defaulting to the current year, a blank month select, a keyword input, and a cover letter toggle checkbox. Selecting a job from the list hydrates both panels without a page reload. Typing in the keyword input filters the visible jobs without a network request and shows the empty-state message when no jobs match. Print preview shows the cover letter on page 1 and the resume beginning on page 2, at Letter size with 0.7in margins.
